basics.name: Huoyuan Tan
basics.label: PhD Student in Robotics
basics.summary: I am a PhD student at Chalmers University of Technology. My research interests include structured, interpretable, and experience-driven robot learning for resilient and adaptive behavior in collaborative robots. I hold an M.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering from the University of Gothenburg and have over five years of industry experience developing and deploying autonomous mobile robotic systems for industrial automation.

work.name: Xingyun Intelligence (Shenzhen) Technology Co., Ltd.
work.summary: Developed and deployed algorithms for autonomous mobile robotic systems used in logistics, factory, and port automation.
highlights: Multi-sensor fusion (camera, LiDAR, GNSS/RTK, IMU), SLAM, perception, planning, control, and ROS-based system development in C++.
Drove end-to-end delivery — from algorithm design and system integration to on-site deployment and fleet tuning — across hardware, software, and operations teams.

publications.name: Simultaneous Indoor Tracking and Activity Recognition Using Pyroelectric Infrared Sensors
publications.summary: 3rd author. X. Luo, Q. Guan, H. Tan, L. Gao, Z. Wang, and X. Luo. Proposed a method for simultaneous indoor tracking and activity recognition using PIR sensor arrays and a two-layer Random Forest classifier.

publications.name: Abnormal Activity Detection Using Pyroelectric Infrared Sensors
publications.summary: 2nd author. X. Luo, H. Tan, Q. Guan, T. Liu, H. Zhuo, and B. Shen. Proposed an unsupervised method for abnormal activity detection using spectral clustering, Hidden Markov Models (HMMs), and One-Class SVMs.

projects.name: PhD Research — Resilient and Adaptive Collaborative Robots
projects.summary: Researching structured, interpretable, and experience-driven robot learning methods that enable collaborative robots to behave resiliently and adapt to new situations.
highlights: CRAFT Lab, Division of Systems and Control, Chalmers University of Technology

projects.name: M.Sc. Thesis — Assessment and Failure Recovery in Remote VLA Deployment
projects.summary: Built a pipeline for deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models remotely, with runtime monitoring and failure recovery for robot manipulation.
highlights: Remote deployment of VLA policies with robot-side execution
Runtime monitoring and assessment of task execution
Evaluation in simulation and on a real robot

projects.name: Autonomous Forklift
projects.summary: Developed an autonomous forklift system integrating onboard sensing, roadside infrastructure, and cloud services for automated unloading of goods from trucks.
highlights: MPC-based motion planning for precise navigation
Achieved 90–92% success rates in automated loading and unloading

projects.name: Intelligent Guided Vehicle (IGV) — Autonomous Port Truck (ART)
projects.summary: Developed autonomous transport robots for container transportation and port automation.
highlights: Multi-LiDAR calibration and sensor fusion (LiDAR, GNSS/RTK, IMU)
Achieved 35 containers/hour throughput in real-world port deployment

projects.name: Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV)
projects.summary: Developed automated guided vehicles for material transportation in factories.
highlights: LiDAR–IMU graph-based SLAM with loop closure
Deployed across indoor and outdoor factory environments

projects.name: Indoor Activity Recognition with Pyroelectric Infrared Sensors
projects.summary: Developed a PIR sensor-based system for indoor tracking and activity monitoring to support older adults living independently.
highlights: Pyroelectric Infrared (PIR) sensor array with FOV modulation
Two-layer Random Forest classifier for tracking and activity recognition
Abnormal activity detection via HMMs and One-Class SVMs
